dqRubric.naRules: The design-quality checklist must not judge redesign of the supplied kit components or double-score exact wording, product records, motif counts, dimensions, layout geometry and reuse requirements covered by these rules.

requirementChecks.criteria: Deliver exactly the 6 named independent items for tier 6. Duplicate exports do not add items. Only six final static artworks are commissioned; no process, video or presentation is required.
Use the explicitly marked final version; if none is marked, use the last exported version.
Each static role is a separate complete export. Multi-view technical boards are allowed where commissioned; do not count one contact sheet or duplicate export as several roles.

Backgrounds read as warm white, product image wells as white, headings as pine green #264C43, and information panels as cream #F5F0E6. Allow ordinary rendering and display differences, but fail a visibly different heading color, panel color or background system.

Each main image identifies its own kit by the correct name, code and USD 24 price. Each shopping card presents both complete records, with USD 24 visibly associated with each individual kit. Swapped names or codes, missing prices, or a price presented as buying both kits fail.

Where a full motif is visible, Fern Study has one upright curved stem and six opposite leaf pairs; Daisy Study has three eight-petal flowers, each with a stem and two leaves. Preprinted and partial views retain the same underlying design. Cropped material or stitch details need not expose the entire motif, but visible elements must agree with their SKU. Missing, extra or substituted motif elements fail.

Full motifs occupy a 100 × 100 mm design area relative to the supplied 150 mm inner hoop diameter and 250 × 250 mm fabric. Use visible component relationships or dimension annotations as evidence; permit perspective and close-up cropping. A full motif visibly enlarged or reduced to an incompatible physical scale fails. Printing a dimension on every image is not required.

The main image is square, detail panels are 2:3 portraits, and the shopping card is 9:16. Each reserves the upper 20% for information and the lower 80% for product imagery on white, keeps content within 5% outer margins, and uses text at least 3% of the shorter side in height. Typography stays in the information band. The main product group spans 85–90% of its image well's width. Judge relative geometry rather than pixel dimensions.

Under the supplied-goods label, the panel accounts for one wooden hoop, one preprinted cotton square, four skeins, two No. 7 needles, one guide and one kraft box. Labels identify the hoop's 150 mm inner and 166 mm outer diameters, 250 × 250 mm fabric, 100 × 140 mm guide, 38 mm needles and 270 × 270 × 35 mm box. The hoop, fabric and guide are depicted at a common scale, allowing perspective but not independent resizing. Missing stock, incorrect quantities or dimensions, and a guide that cannot function as the stated scale reference fail.

The readable sequence mounts the preprinted fabric, separates two strands and threads the needle, stitches the motif, then finishes the back. Preparation visibly distinguishes two working strands from the six-strand source. The finishing stage shows trimming and gathering behind the hoop. Scissors are associated with 'You supply: scissors'. Reordered or missing stages, an ambiguous strand split, or scissors presented as supplied stock fail.

The finished panel shows a fully stitched Fern Study with all twelve leaves. The comparison card shows complete Fern and Daisy outcomes, including eight petals on each of Daisy's three flowers. 'Finished example - stitch it yourself' is attached to the panel's outcome and separately to each completed motif on the card. A single ambiguous card-level label, unfinished examples presented as finished, or completed embroidery presented as supplied merchandise fails.

The material panel reveals cotton weave and the needle pair, and gives four complete records: T01 Pine #365744, T02 Sage #90A889, T03 Cream #F3E9D2 and T04 Ochre #C99236, each 8 m and six-strand, plus two No. 7 needles. Across relevant views, preserve the reference components' pale nested wooden hoop and brass screw, cream cotton and gray printing, separate skeins with cream wraps, silver needles, white four-stage guide and shallow kraft box. Fern uses an Ochre stem, Sage left leaves, Pine right leaves and Cream veins. Daisy uses Pine stems and veins, Sage leaves, Cream petals and Ochre centers. Permit changes in viewpoint and stitching progress; fail changed component identities, swapped thread assignments or incomplete material records.

The six images use a coherent shop system of heading treatment, information panels, typography and spacing while adapting to their required proportions. Repeated Fern components and motifs retain their identities and recorded color assignments through unstitched, instructional and completed views; Daisy remains a distinct, correctly represented comparison kit. The combined imagery distinguishes the supplied starter-kit materials, buyer-supplied scissors and embroidery that the buyer must complete.
